ground_stay.notes: 113 CONTINUOUS DAYS on the Provo ramp - the longest published stay by any aircraft in this investigation, covering 10 September. Only local flights were flown during it: Provo-Provo on 10 Jun and a 1:08 Provo-Provo on 5 Sep. Audit: 'ACCURATE POSS BROKEN JET GROUNDED IN PROVO' and 'ONLY LOCAL FLIGHTS WERE FLOWN IN AND AROUND PROVO FROM 10 JUNE-13 SEPT.' Owens: transponder ON on 10 Sep but the aircraft DID NOT TAKE OFF. COUNTERARGUMENT: a four-month stay is a maintenance-visit length, not a surveillance-orbit length. THE OWENS SHEET'S 7 JUL 2025 'GOOSEBAY-PARIS-CAIRO' ROW IS ENTERED TWICE (index 37 and 66) AND BOTH ARE FALSE - the aircraft was here the whole time.

THE DEPARTURE TIME IS DISPUTED THREE WAYS AND THEY CANNOT ALL BE TRUE: (a) wheels-up ~07:08-07:14 MT, roughly five hours BEFORE the shot, per the Flightradar24 export; (b) Candace Owens's 'nuclear flight logs' - power-up 9:05 am, track goes dark, reactivates 17 minutes after the shot, idles to 1:29 pm; (c) @ProjectConstitu / @nihilox - it never left Provo at all and launched from Dugway Proving Ground's Michael Army Airfield with the transponder off until clear of R-6404. Part of the spread is a UTC-versus-local conversion error circulating uncorrected (13:08 UTC = 07:08 MDT, published as both). SU-BND's unexplained 68-minute Provo->Provo sortie on 5 Sept has an exact twin: SU-BGM flew a 55-minute Provo->Provo loop on 10 Apr 2025 - the signature of a post-maintenance functional check flight. If the September loop is anomalous, consistency requires treating the April one the same way. Duncan Aviation's Egyptian Air Force account dates to 1999.

From 23 May to 13 Sept 2025 - 113 continuous days - a foreign-registered jet was parked at this field, and in those 113 days SU-BND flew exactly twice, both Provo->Provo round-robins.
